questions.question: Which statement describes matter?
choices: It consists only of visible solids
It has energy but no mass
It has mass and occupies space

questions.question: Which property is independent of sample amount?
Which is an example of a physical property?
Which is an example of a chemical property?
Which change is physical?
Which change forms new substances?
choices: A change in sample size only

questions.question: How is density calculated?
Why does melting generally leave a substance's chemical identity unchanged?
choices: Its particles rearrange without becoming a different substance
Its elements change during every melting event

questions.question: Why is reversibility alone insufficient to classify a change as physical?
choices: No physical change can be reversed
All irreversible changes form new elements
Some chemical changes can be reversed, and some physical changes are hard to reverse

questions.question: Why should temperature be specified when comparing densities?
choices: Temperature changes the definition of mass
All materials have equal density at one temperature
Temperature can affect volume and therefore density

questions.question: What distinguishes mass from volume?
choices: Mass measures occupied space; volume measures matter
Mass measures matter; volume measures occupied space
Both measure the same property in different units
Volume is measured only in kilograms

questions.question: Why can a color change alone be inconclusive evidence of a chemical change?
choices: Only chemical changes can affect color
Color change always means an element has changed
Physical mixing can also change apparent color
Color change always means the original material lost mass

questions.question: What usually happens to density when the mass and volume of a uniform sample are both doubled under unchanged conditions?
Why is burning wood a chemical change?
choices: Its components react to form different substances

questions.question: Why is crushing a mineral generally a physical change?
choices: Its size changes while its chemical composition can stay the same
Its atoms must become a different element
Its chemical bonds must all disappear

questions.question: A sample has mass 24 g and volume 8 cm³. What is its density?
A uniform material has density 2 g/cm³ and volume 5 cm³. What is its mass?
A liquid freezes without reacting. Which classification fits?
A solid reacts with a gas and forms a substance with new properties. What best supports a chemical-change classification?
choices: A change in the sample's location

questions.question: Two samples have the same density but different masses. What can be concluded?
choices: They may be the same material with different volumes
They must occupy the same volume
The heavier one must have greater density
